summary: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology in Saudi Arabia is a graduate-only research university in science and engineering. More than nine in ten admitted students receive the KAUST Fellowship, which pays tuition, a stipend, housing, health insurance and relocation.
meta_description: KAUST funds most admitted master's and PhD students: tuition, a $20,000–30,000 stipend, housing and health cover. Eligibility, fields and the deadline.
covers: Full tuition and bench fees, worth up to $35,000 a year.
A stipend of $20,000 a year for master's students and $25,000 to $30,000 for PhD students, depending on qualifications and progress.
Campus housing: shared for single students, a two-bedroom unit for married students.
Health insurance for you and dependants living on campus, and relocation support for the visa and travel.
eligibility: Applicants to a master's, master's/PhD or PhD programme in science or engineering at KAUST.
Admission is merit-based, after a faculty assessment and possibly an interview.
Students with outside sponsorship that pays a stipend may not be eligible for the fellowship.
how_to_apply: Choose your programme on KAUST's admissions site and check its requirements.
Apply online in the round for your intake; for autumn 2027 the deadline is 3 January 2027 (tentative).
Upload transcripts, references, test scores and a statement of purpose.
Shortlisted applicants are invited to interview; decisions for this round are due on 14 February 2027.
watch_out: Programmes are in science, engineering and computing only.
You cannot hold another full scholarship that pays a stipend alongside the KAUST Fellowship.
Round dates are tentative and can change, so check the admissions timeline before you apply.
